title: Hash-anchored TFState + tenant-claim orchestrator for GPU nodepool modules
author: Sophia Chen
description: Context: Private installs require predictable, shardable tfstate boundaries for tenant-scoped GPU node pools and network attachments. Current monolithic state caused long plan/apply times and frequent lock contention during tenant onboarding. This PR introduces a hash-anchored tfstate layout plus a lightweight tenant-claim orchestrator to (1) create tenant-scoped state slices for GPU pools and associated subnet leases, (2) deterministically derive tenant IAM role names/ARNs to avoid drift, and (3) provide a reversible migration path with automated backups and a rollback driver.
motivation_and_goals: Primary goals: reduce tf plan/app latency for tenant onboarding; eliminate cross-tenant lock contention; provide a safe migration from existing consolidated state to sharded, anchored state; surface deterministic naming to downstream installers so IAM and RBAC can be reconciled without manual intervention.
summary_of_changes:
- New module: modules/tfstate-anchor (creates per-tenant state objects named by sha1(tenant_id||cluster_id||env) and exposes state bucket/object metadata.
- New module: modules/tenant-claim-orchestrator (statemachine that claims subnets, creates GPU pool resources in tenant-scoped state, emits lease tokens).
- Updates to modules/gpu-pool: split resource creation into local 'proxy' move and remote state-backed resources; added lifecycle prevent_destroy on critical subnet attachments.
- Updated modules/iam: deterministic role naming and policy templating to avoid manual lookups.
- Migration tooling: scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh and docs/migrations/anchor-migration.md with dry-run and preview modes.
- CI: added integration test harness for multi-tenant plan/app and lock contention simulation.
- Added reconciliation hook for private-installer to call the orchestrator during tenant create flow.

migration_plan: 1) Dry-run mode: run scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh --preview against a staging copy of the state bucket to validate generated anchors and import mapping; 2) Backup: script creates dated snapshots in s3://redwood-tfstate-backups/<date>/ and verifies checksums; 3) Lease handoff: orchestrator claims subnets and creates tenant-scoped state; 4) Import: run terraform import commands emitted by the migration script to move resources to new state slices; 5) Promote: update private-installer to point to tenant-scoped remote state and remove deprecated central references; 6) Monitor: run integration smoke tests and metric checks for 24h. Rollback path included: restore snapshot and re-register central state, orchestrator will release leases on revert.
rollback_and_safety:
- Automatic snapshot before any destructive changes.
- Import preview mode to capture mapping without state mutation.
- Orchestrator has a reversible 'claim' step: a lease token can be revoked and resources remain untouched until 'promote' is called.
- Added extra CI gate to prevent merges if migration scripts are in an unreviewed state.
- Documented manual rollback commands in docs/migrations/anchor-migration.md.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for templated IAM names, integration test that simulates 10 concurrent tenant onboard flows to assert no lock contention, end-to-end verify that subnet leases are unique and that GPU pool create is successful using remote state. Also added a chaos test that kills the orchestrator mid-claim to validate idempotency. All tests included in CI pipeline.
release_notes:
- Introduced hash-anchored tfstate layout for tenant-scoped GPU pools and subnet leases; reduces plan/app contention and accelerates tenant onboarding.
- New tenant-claim-orchestrator module to safely claim subnets and create tenant-scoped resources.
- Deterministic IAM role naming to prevent drift and simplify RBAC reconciliation.
- Migration tooling (dry-run, backup, import steps) and rollback path.
- Integration tests and observability hooks for migration and orchestrator metrics.
